correctness.rationale: At R₀φ=1 choose Z=exp(∫₀ᵗJ), so Ż=ZJ. Using population conservation and the two never-infected equations shows that ZJ+sZ^(−α)+vZ^(−ε) is conserved and equals 1 from the initial data, with α=(1−φ)/φ and ε=(θ−φ)/φ. Hence i≤Ż≤1 and 1+it≤Z≤1+t. At fixed ε, Ż and Z/t tend to the same strictly positive constant (1−v or 1), giving tJ→1. Independently, total recovered fraction R satisfies Ṙ=J−JR and Q̇=JR, so Q=log Z−R, counting only postinitial reinfections. This gives exactly the two offsets. For T=exp(z/ε), fixed z>0 and r>0, the linear bounds give ε log Z(rT)→z and Z(rT)^(−α)→0. Averaging Ż over [0,T] by bounded convergence gives Z(T)/T→1−v exp(−z); R(T)→1 by the same bounds. This proves the asserted profile including its additive constant and the order of the limits.
residual_risks: No statement at z=0 before the limit or uniform error rate is established. Finite trajectory diagnostics cannot certify a double-limit theorem. The calculation does not cover finite stochastic populations.

originality.rationale: The leaky-vaccination equations and integrating-factor prevalence relation are prior, and the critical 1/t tail is not a standalone originality basis. The distinctive finding is the matched cumulative-reinfection offsets and the sharp exponential-time interpolation as the two susceptibility parameters coalesce at the exact reinfection threshold. The closest full text supplies the state relation but does not give this singular clock or a result implying it without additional analysis.
residual_risks: Literature comparison is bounded and not a priority certification. Full texts of the older Katriel and Gomes papers were unavailable, so their precise simpler-model critical asymptotics remain unchecked.

value.rationale: The exact reinfection threshold and equality of two existing model susceptibilities are natural boundaries. The common 1/t prevalence tail hides a discontinuity in an integrated event-count offset. The exponential-time profile explains how that discrepancy builds up and identifies the precise limit missed by treating the small parameter at fixed observation time or in fixed-parameter final-size analysis.
residual_risks: The result is a deterministic critical-model benchmark, not a prediction for a finite population, a vaccine recommendation, or an inference from reported counts.
